title: Time
subtitle: in time, for ages, it takes
summary: Use the common phrases and prepositions of time correctly, and say how long something takes or lasts.

lesson.heading: Phrases with time
lesson.text: A small group of fixed phrases with **time** is used every day. Learn them as whole phrases.

examples.text: We got to the meeting **in time**.
Do you **have time** for a cup of coffee?
examples.note: = have enough time to do something

examples.text: Call me **the next time** you're in London.
Sophie and I arrived **at the same time**, 9 o'clock exactly.

left.label: until
left.text: Something continues up to that moment.
examples: We can't leave **until** the others get back.

right.label: by
examples: The teacher told us to finish our homework **by** Monday.

lesson.heading: Prepositions people often confuse
rows: a point in time in the past
I worked on a farm **during** the summer.
I worked on a farm **for** a month. (not ~~during a month~~)
I'm going back to Brazil **in ten days' time**. (not ~~after ten days~~)

lesson.heading: Approximate periods of time
rows: for a long time, e.g. many years
in the last few weeks or months
I haven't been to the dentist **recently**.
e.g. five to ten years ago
I used to go skiing, but that was **a long time ago**.
a few days ago, perhaps a week
My sister went to the zoo **the other day**.
a period including the past and now
I don't see my brother much **these days**.
This dictionary's fine **for the time being**.
in the future, but I don't know when
I'm sure I'll go to America **one day**.

left.label: take
left.text: How long you need to do something.
examples: It **takes** me half an hour to get to school.
We can walk, but it'll **take** us a long time.

right.label: last
right.text: How long something continues, from beginning to end.
examples: The battery in my camera didn't **last** long.

lesson.text: **On time** = punctual; **in time** = early enough. He was **on time** for the train, so he got there **in time** to buy a ticket.

exercises.prompt: The shop closes at 5.30. If we don't hurry, we'll never get there ___ time.
exercises.explanation: In time = early enough, before something happens.

exercises.prompt: I always get to meetings ___ time; I hate it when people are late.
exercises.explanation: On time = not early and not late.

exercises.prompt: I'm afraid I won't ___ time to see you this week.
exercises.explanation: Have time to do something = have enough time for it.

exercises.prompt: Julian and I got to the station at the ___ time.
exercises.explanation: At the same time = together, at the same moment.

exercises.prompt: We can't leave ___ the others get back.
I've been in the army ___ I was eighteen.
exercises.explanation: Since + a point in time in the past.

exercises.prompt: I visit my uncle every week ___ the winter.
exercises.explanation: During tells you when; for tells you how long.

exercises.prompt: She's going back to France ___ three months' time.
exercises.explanation: We say in three months' time, not ~~after three months~~.

exercises.prompt: I went to Egypt with my parents, but that was ten years ago - a long time ___.
exercises.explanation: A long time ago (syn ages ago) = many years ago.

exercises.prompt: I went to the library three days ago - the ___ day, in fact.
exercises.explanation: The other day = a few days ago, perhaps a week.

exercises.prompt: This computer will be fine for the next year, so it's good enough for the time ___.
exercises.explanation: For the time being = for now, the near future.

exercises.statement: It lasts me half an hour to get to school.
exercises.explanation: It takes me half an hour to get to school. Use take for how long you need to do something.

exercises.prompt: Match each period of time with how long it is.
